text: Skills, tools and a shared knowledge base that let any AI coding agent mod almost any PC game you own.
The agent finds the game, works out the engine and the route, reads the real code, builds the mod, makes art, 3D and sound
with fal, tests it in the running game, cuts the video, and writes down what it learned for the next agent.
Coming next: the mod hub. Publish your mods, remix other people's, and make new ones.
Share what you make, get help, and follow along:
## PAYDAY 2 — Miranda Lawson (LAS outfit)
Miranda Lawson ships as a **Legendary Armour Skins (LAS) add-on** — an
equipable, full-body outfit with its own units and first-person arms (the
`2b.rar` product shape), built through **two complementary routes**:
**1. ME2 COLLADA route — primary, released.** Built by `tools/pd2-port/`, a
rigged-COLLADA → LAS pipeline that is not tied to this character: Miranda is
the port it ships, and [its README](tools/pd2-port/README.md) lists what a
port of another character changes. Source: `models/PC _ Computer - Mass
Effect 2 - Non-Playable Characters - Miranda Lawson (Romance).zip` (rigged
COLLADA + textures). Output is
`dist/lawson_las.zip` (tracked), installed to **`PAYDAY 2\assets\mod_overrides\`**
and requiring **SuperBLT + BeardLib + Legendary Armour Skins / Wardrobe**.
Audited against the ModWorkshop LAS/MOOG guide on every build
(`check_guide_compliance.py`: 38 pass / 1 warn / 0 fail, the auditor itself
mutation-tested) and guarded against winding defects that leave holes in the
skin. Release: [`lawson-las-v2`](https://github.com/Man1nWhite/universal-modder/releases/tag/lawson-las-v2).
Current state, open problems and workflow traps:
[`tools/pd2-port/STATUS.md`](tools/pd2-port/STATUS.md).
**2. L4D2 Source route — parallel line.** `tools/pd2-las/`, built from
`models/l4d2_miranda_lawson_1.zip` (an L4D2 Miranda replacement for Rochelle)
onto the 2B template skeleton. Output `dist/Miranda_LAS.zip` (tracked in `dist/` and
`build/pd2-las/Miranda_LAS.zip` with `.sha256` checksums), installed to
**`PAYDAY 2\assets\mod_overrides\`** like 2B itself. Agents start at
[`tools/pd2-las/README.md`](tools/pd2-las/README.md) (status command, build
commands, invariants); the dated state, in-game results and dead ends are in
[`docs/pd2-las/HANDOFF.md`](docs/pd2-las/HANDOFF.md).
**3. Heister Head-Replacement `mod_overrides` (Joy, Clover, Bonnie, Sydney, and Geralt over Rust).**
`tools/build_joy_head_mods.py` builds standalone `mod_overrides` head-replacement packages:
- **Miranda Lawson** (both L4D2 and ME2 Romance sources) over **Joy, Clover, Bonnie, and Sydney**:
`dist/Miranda_{L4D2,Romance}_over_{Joy,Clover,Bonnie,Sydney}.zip` (8 packages).
- **Geralt of Rivia** (built from `models/Geralt.7z`, Witcher 3 L4D2 port) over **Rust (`npc_criminal_wild_1`)**:

`dist/Geralt_over_Rust.zip` (2-atom `mtr_head` + `ALPHA_MASKED` `mtr_hair` setup with `2048x2048` face/eyes/teeth and hair/beard/eyelashes atlases, heist + menu `.model`, 3 `.material_config` files, and B&W HUD/Menu icon).

All packages include `.sha256` sidecars in `dist/` and rendered 4-angle preview sheets in `docs/previews/` (`00_all_miranda_mods_overview.png` .. `11_Geralt_over_Rust.png`, plus `12_Miranda_Busty_LAS.png` with its `13_Miranda_Busty_vs_LAS_chest.png` before/after close-ups (0–90°) and `14_Miranda_Busty_vs_LAS_top_below.png` overhead/underside pair).
What each Miranda pack replaces: Clover and Bonnie cover the heist model, the
menu model, *and* the Safe House (`*_chill`) model; Joy and Sydney cover the
heist and menu models only, so their Safe House unit keeps the vanilla head.
The four **L4D2** packs (`Miranda_L4D2_over_{Joy,Clover,Bonnie,Sydney}.zip`)
were **tested in game on 2026-11-05** (user-side check). The Romance variants
and `Geralt_over_Rust.zip` are still unverified in game — the only in-game
checklist in the repo is the LAS one,
[`docs/pd2-las/in-game-checklist.md`](docs/pd2-las/in-game-checklist.md).
Audit of this set: [`docs/audits/2026-11-05-head-pack-audit.md`](docs/audits/2026-11-05-head-pack-audit.md).
Both LAS lines follow the ModWorkshop Wiki
[LAS/MOOG/Outfit Module Guide](https://wiki.modworkshop.net/books/payday-2-mod-creation/page/legendary-armor-skinslasmoogoutfit-module-guide).
The tool trees stay separate by design; [`tools/README.md`](tools/README.md)
records why and where the boundary is.
The earlier approach that surgically replaced heister character models
(Clover/Bonnie/Sydney, plus outfit packs built on the same mesh) was **retired
as a dead end** on 2026-10-18: the source rig was broken, the packs crashed or
rendered wrong in-game, and the model-editing pipeline was not reproducible
from a clean checkout. Audits:
[route change (LAS line)](docs/audits/2026-10-18-route-change-audit.md) ·
[old model retired (ME2 line)](docs/audits/2026-10-18-old-model-retired-las-restart.md).
## Install
Pick your agent. Each gets the same skills (Agent Skills format), the fal MCP server, and the `um` CLI.
| Agent | Install |

| **Claude Code** | `/plugin marketplace add rehan-remade/universal-modder`
`/plugin install universal-modder@universal-modder` |

| **Codex** | `codex plugin marketplace add rehan-remade/universal-modder`
`codex plugin add universal-modder@universal-modder` |
| **Gemini CLI** | `gemini extensions install https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder` |
| **VS Code / Copilot** | Enable `chat.plugins.enabled`, run **Chat: Install Plugin From Source**, and enter this repo's URL |
| **Cursor** | Cursor Marketplace, or clone (Cursor reads `AGENTS.md` and `.cursor/mcp.json`) |

| **OpenCode** | Clone and run `opencode` inside it (`opencode.json` adds the skills and the fal MCP server)
or, on OpenCode 2, `opencode plugin add 'github:rehan-remade/universal-modder#main::path:plugins/opencode'` (the `um` tool and fal MCP; add the skills with **Skills only**) |

| **Skills only**
(any agent) | `npx skills add https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder` |
| **Anything else** | `git clone https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder` and start your agent inside it |
Inside a clone, each agent finds the skills where it looks for them: `.agents/skills` (Codex, Gemini CLI,
Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode) and `.claude/skills` (Claude Code) are copies of `skills/`. Instructions are in
`AGENTS.md`, which `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` point to. MCP config is in `.mcp.json`, `.codex/config.toml`,
`.cursor/mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json` and `opencode.json` (which also points OpenCode at `skills/`).
Without a clone, OpenCode 2 installs the plugin in `plugins/opencode/` with `opencode plugin add`: one
`um_run` tool that passes its arguments straight to the CLI and runs `um` from PATH (see below), plus the
fal MCP server when `FAL_KEY` is set and none is configured. A clone doesn't need it. See
`plugins/opencode/README.md`.
**The `um` CLI.** Plugin installs and clones put it on PATH (OpenCode's plugin install doesn't). Anywhere else:
```bash
uv tool install git+https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder     # or: pipx install git+...
**For assets,** get a [fal API key](https://fal.ai/dashboard/keys). It powers both the fal MCP server and
`um fal`. Rather than exporting it from a shell profile or a `.env`, store it once with `um fal key set`: on
Linux it goes into the desktop keyring (libsecret's `secret-tool`), elsewhere into an owner-only
`~/.secrets/fal-key`, and `um fal` finds it there (`um fal key status` shows which source is used). `FAL_KEY`
in the environment still works and wins. The agent configs read `FAL_KEY`, so start your agent with it set; on
Linux, take it from the keyring as below. With no key, fal's OAuth endpoint `https://mcp.fal.ai/mcp-relay`
signs you in through the browser instead ([fal's MCP guides](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/setting-up/mcp)),
and `um comfy` makes images on a local ComfyUI server.
```bash
um fal key set                                                   # hidden prompt
export FAL_KEY="$(secret-tool lookup service fal.ai key api)"    # Linux: before starting the agent
You also need Git, Python 3.10+ and ffmpeg. `uv` is recommended. Blender is needed for 3D → sprite renders.
Windows games are driven natively or from WSL.
## Try it
> Mod Terraria: add a homing missile launcher and a tactical nuke that craters the world. Make the sprites with fal.
> Make a new civilization for Age of Empires II with a unique unit rendered from 3D.
> Put real Minecraft inside GTA V story mode. Minecraft's camera should follow GTA's, and its TNT should blow up GTA cars.
> Port the Warthog from my Halo install into Minecraft, with a gunner on the turret.
> What engine is `C:\Games\Foo`, and has anyone modded it before?
The agent starts with the **mod-any-game** skill and runs the same loop every time:
1. search the knowledge base;
2. recon, then pick a route;
3. set up a safe lab (saves backed up);
4. read the actual code;
5. build one working slice;
6. generate assets;
7. verify in the real game;
8. record;
9. package;
10. write a field note for the next agent.
## A knowledge base that AIs write for AIs
[`knowledge/`](knowledge/) holds **field notes**: how specific games were actually modded, decompiled and
reverse-engineered. Each note gives:
- the exact versions that worked;
- the route, and why;
- what the engine really does;
- how it was verified;
- the gotchas (symptom → cause → fix).
**Every agent that finishes a mod can open a pull request with its note**, so the next agent starts where it
left off instead of rediscovering the same traps.
```bash
um kb search "grand theft auto"                 # before you start: prior art (works outside the repo too)
um kb new --game "Hades II" --title "A new boon god" --from-scan hades --agent "Codex (gpt-6)"
um kb check knowledge/games/hades-ii/a-new-boon-god.md
um kb pr knowledge/games/hades-ii/a-new-boon-god.md --yes    # after your human says OK: branch, push, PR
Browse [`knowledge/INDEX.md`](knowledge/INDEX.md). Every game is welcome. Contribution rules, for humans and
AIs, are in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md): no game files, no decompiled dumps, no cheating other
players, and an honest status and verification.

## Rules it follows
- **Any game you own: single-player, multiplayer, or servers you host.** It refuses to inject into online
games with anti-cheat, write cheats against other players, or bypass anti-cheat, DRM or ownership checks.
- **It never ships game files or decompiled code.** Mods ship as code, your own assets, patches or
converters.
- **It backs up before touching saves**, and kills processes by PID only.
- **It asks before** driving your mouse and keyboard, installing loaders into game folders, or publishing,
PRs included.
Full reasoning: [`skills/mod-any-game/references/safety.md`](skills/mod-any-game/references/safety.md).

## Star history
# universal-modder
A game-modding toolkit and a shared knowledge base for AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini
CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode and anything else that reads `AGENTS.md`. When someone opens an agent in this
repo, they almost always want to **mod a game**, or to learn how a game was modded.
## Start here
1. **Read `skills/mod-any-game/SKILL.md` and follow its loop:** intake → recon → route → lab (backups) →
source of truth → vertical slice → assets → verify in the real game → showcase → publish.
2. **Search the knowledge base first:** `bin/um kb search "<game or engine>"`. Other agents may already have
written down the exact versions, routes and gotchas (`knowledge/INDEX.md`).
3. **On a long-running project, keep a status page:** the agent that picks
the work up next should not have to reconstruct the state from a journal.
The COLLADA → LAS pipeline in `tools/pd2-port/` keeps one for the port it
ships at `tools/pd2-port/STATUS.md` (shipped artefacts, measured check
results, the open problem, the traps) next to its journal, and
`tools/pd2-las/status.py` prints the state of its tree as JSON — copy
those patterns.
4. **At the end, share what you learned:** write a field note (`bin/um kb new ...`) and, once your human
agrees, open a PR (`bin/um kb pr <note> --yes`). See `knowledge/README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
## Tools
- **`bin/um`** is the Python CLI, and it sets itself up with `uv`.
- Put it on PATH: `export PATH="$PWD/bin:$PATH"` (from Windows cmd or PowerShell, add `bin` to PATH and
`bin\um.cmd` runs it), or install it anywhere with
`uv tool install git+https://github.com/rehan-remade/universal-modder`.
- Every group has `--help`:
- `scan`: installed games, engine, anti-cheat, loaders, saves, routes
- `fal`: sprites, textures, PBR, 3D, rigs, SFX, music, voice, video via fal's REST API
- `comfy`: images from a local ComfyUI server, with no API key
- `sprite` / `render3d`: art → engine-ready frames (`render3d` needs Blender on PATH or `BLENDER=...`)
- `win`: launch, screenshot, input, record on Windows (also from WSL)
- `video`: contact sheets and EDL showcase edits
- `backup`: snapshot and restore saves
- `publish`: pre-release lint
- `kb`: the knowledge base
- **fal MCP server:** `https://mcp.fal.ai/mcp` with header `Authorization: Bearer $FAL_KEY`.
- It's pre-configured per agent: `.mcp.json` (Claude Code), `.codex/config.toml` (Codex),
`.cursor/mcp.json` (Cursor), `.vscode/mcp.json` (VS Code / Copilot), `gemini-extension.json`
(Gemini CLI), `opencode.json` (OpenCode).
- It needs `FAL_KEY` in the agent's environment; without it the server doesn't connect. fal's OAuth
endpoint, `https://mcp.fal.ai/mcp-relay`, takes a browser sign-in instead (see `skills/fal-assets`).
- No MCP? `um fal` does the same over REST. It also finds the key that `um fal key set` stored (the
desktop keyring on Linux, `~/.secrets/fal-key` elsewhere).
- **Skills** (`skills/*/SKILL.md`, Agent Skills format) are copied where agents look for them in a clone:
`.agents/skills` (Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode) and `.claude/skills` (Claude Code). Edit
`skills/`, then copy it over; a test fails while the copies differ.
- **Engine playbooks:** `skills/mod-any-game/references/engines/`.
- **Worked examples:** `examples/terraria-tmodloader`, `examples/aoe2-de-civ`,
`examples/minecraft-gta5-passthrough`, `examples/outer-wilds-portal-gun`, `examples/mindustry-homing`,
`examples/cities-skylines-city-dashboard`.
## Rules (full reasoning in `skills/mod-any-game/references/safety.md`)
- **What you can mod:** any game the user owns: single-player, multiplayer, or servers the user hosts.
- Never touch online clients protected by anti-cheat.
- Never write cheats against other players (aimbots, ESP, speed hacks).
- Never bypass anti-cheat, DRM or ownership checks.
- **Saves:** `um backup` saves before modded launches.
- **What you ship:** never commit or publish game files, extracted assets or decompiled code. Keep
decompiles outside the repo.
- **Processes:** kill by exact PID (`um win kill`), never by name pattern.
- **Ask first** before:
- driving the user's mouse and keyboard, and never focus a game with an online mode while they're typing;
- installing loaders into game folders or changing the registry;
- publishing anything, PRs included.
- **Keep a journal:** a `MODLOG.md` in the mod's working folder. It becomes your field note at the end.
- **Sequence your file edits:** parallel edits to the same file race, and the
loser silently clobbers the winner.
## Working on the toolkit itself
- **Python:** 3.10+, deps Pillow, numpy and PyYAML (`uv` handles them via `bin/um`). Code lives in `um/`,
one module per CLI group, each with `register(sub)` and a docstring that doubles as `--help`.
- **Windows tools:** `um/ps1/*.ps1` embed C# 5 (Windows PowerShell 5.1's compiler): no string
interpolation, no `out var`, no expression-bodied members.
- **Tests:** `uv run --with pytest pytest -q tests`. CI also runs `um kb check --index` and
`um publish check .`.
- **Wording:** keep skills and docs agent-neutral ("the agent", not a product name) except in sections
about one specific agent.

A restarted sandbox comes back without `.venv/` and without anything under `dist/`, `build/` and `node_modules/`, tracked files included, so `git status` lists the packs as deleted. `git checkout -- dist build node_modules` restores them and `make -sC tools/pd2-las env` rebuilds the pinned `.venv` and unpacks the 2B templates; `python3 tools/pd2-las/status.py` says which of the two is still missing. Earlier sessions also found local `HEAD` rewound behind the pushed branch. Only in that case, and only after `git status` and `git log origin/<branch>..HEAD` show nothing local that the remote lacks, `git reset --hard origin/<branch>`: a reset discards commits and edits that were never pushed, so it is never the first step.
### Critical Diesel Engine & PAYDAY 2 Invariants (Do Not Break)
These hold in every pipeline. A pipeline's own invariants, and the tests that enforce them, are in its entry point above.
1. **Two Diesel `.model` Parsers**:

- `tools/pd2-las/diesel_model.py` (`dm.ModelFile.read` + `dm.decode_geometry` / `dm.decode_topology` / `dm.decode_model_data`) decodes any legacy PAYDAY 2 `.model` (`2b.model`, `miranda.model`, `npc_criminal_joy_1.model`).
- `tools/pd2-port/dmodel.py` (`DieselModel.from_bytes`) only populates `geo.weights3` for the models `tools/pd2-port/las_model.py` writes (such as `lawson.model`).
2. **Global `Topology` Indices in Multi-Atom Drawables**:

- In Diesel `.model` files (`npc_criminal_joy_1.model`, `miranda.model`), triangle indices in `Topology` for `RenderAtom` `i` are **global vertex indices** in `[base_vertex, base_vertex + slice_len - 1]`, never local `0 .. slice_len - 1`.
3. **UV Coordinate Convention (`v_diesel = 1.0 - v_img`)**:
- Diesel `Geometry.uv0` stores OpenGL/COLLADA bottom-up `v` (`v = 1.0` is top row `y_img = 0` of the DDS image; `v = 0.0` is bottom row `y_img = H - 1`).
- When packing a 2×2 atlas at top-down quadrant `(qx, qy) ∈ {0, 1}²`, map `u_diesel = 0.5 * qx + 0.5 * u_img` and `v_diesel = 1.0 - (0.5 * qy + 0.5 * v_img)`.
4. **DXT5 Diffuse Alpha = Specular/Gloss & DXT5nm Normal Maps**:

- In `generic:...:DIFFUSE_TEXTURE:NORMALMAP:...` shaders (without `ALPHA_MASKED`), the diffuse texture's alpha channel is **gloss/specular intensity** (`alpha = 255` makes skin/fabric look like wet plastic in-game). Keep diffuse alpha low (`<= 28` or normal-slope attenuated).

- Diesel normal maps are **DXT5** with X in alpha and Y in green (Y+: a DirectX-style source has its green inverted). The shader reads only those two channels; both writers here, `dds.pd2_normal_channels(arr, invert_y=True)` in `tools/pd2-port/` and `swizzle_source_normal_dxt5_to_pd2` in `tools/pd2-las/dds_encode.py`, fill red with 255 and blue with 0.
5. **Standing-Pose Shoulder/Arm Alignment & Elbow Hinge Axis (Full-Body LAS)**:

- PAYDAY 2's in-game standing pose swings `RightShoulder`/`LeftShoulder` ~19° downward from bind pose (`z: 147→142 cm`). Retargeting must align clavicle/upper-arm/forearm directions in the **animated standing pose**, and the elbow has to bend about the axis PD2 bends it about so it never shears.

- On the PD2 rig that axis is the `ForeArm`'s **local Y**. Measured on the 2B skeleton: the bind elbow is bent 72.1°, local Y is the normal of that bend, and local X runs along the forearm, so a rotation about X is a twist that leaves the elbow angle unchanged (`docs/pd2-las/CHRISTIE.md`, "The elbow, measured on the elbow's own axis").
6. **Joy Head-Replacement (`mod_overrides`) Collar & Skinning Contract**:

- `npc_criminal_joy_1.model` (`and identical npc_criminal_joy_1_menu.model`) uses `g_head_mask_off` (`id=120`, `geo=228`, `topo=229`) and `g_head` (`id=121`, `geo=233`, `topo=234`), both bound to `SkinBones 44` (`['Spine2', 'Neck', 'Head']`).

- Joy's `g_body` hoodie collar (`z ∈ [151, 160]`) is weighted `95.5%` to `Spine2` (`0% Neck`), with an inner collar cone at `y ≈ 7.2–8.5 cm` and outer V-neck lapel at `y ∈ [12.9, 15.5] cm`. Keep lower-throat vertices in the collar channel `y ∈ [9.0, 10.6] cm` and weight `z <= 156 cm` `100%` to `Spine2` so the neck never separates from the collar when `Neck`/`Head` rotate.
